paper_title: Local Treewidth of Random and Noisy Graphs with Applications to Stopping Contagion in Networks
classifications: Theory of computation → Dynamic graph algorithms
statement: The algorithm above can become slow if r or t are very large. Additionally, we do not know how to get similar results (e.g., algorithms of running time 2|A| poly(n)) for stopping contagion. Below we show that we can improve upon this algorithm for graphs that have some local sparsity conditions. A key property we use is that for both minimizing contagion and stopping contagion with a seed set A, we restrict our attention to the subgraph of G induced on ⟨A⟩.
